content.value_statement: Crypto market data integrations require correct endpoints, authentication, and rate-limit handling. This skill provides CoinGecko API guidance, examples, and workflow prompts for coding agents.
actual_capabilities: Explains CoinGecko public and Pro API authentication methods.
Maps common cryptocurrency market data needs to CoinGecko endpoints.
Guides setup for CoinGecko MCP servers in supported AI clients.
Provides SDK usage patterns for TypeScript and Python integrations.
Summarizes endpoint families for coins, NFTs, exchanges, trending data, and onchain DEX data.
Highlights rate limits, API key handling, and plan-specific access notes.
limitations: It is a documentation skill and does not call the CoinGecko API directly.
It cannot create, validate, or recover CoinGecko API keys.
Market data may change after the bundled documentation snapshot.
It should not be used as financial, trading, tax, or legal advice.

use_cases.title: Build a Crypto Price Tracker
use_cases.description: Find the right price endpoints, authentication method, and response fields for a tracker or dashboard.

use_cases.title: Configure CoinGecko MCP Access
use_cases.description: Compare public, authenticated, and local MCP server options before configuring an AI client.

use_cases.title: Plan Token and NFT Data Workflows
use_cases.description: Identify endpoint groups for token metadata, NFT collections, exchanges, trending assets, and onchain pools.

prompt_templates.title: Find the Right Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: I need CoinGecko data for [asset or market need]. Which endpoint should I use, and what parameters are required?

prompt_templates.title: Design an API Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a CoinGecko API request for [goal]. Include authentication choice, required parameters, and common errors to handle.

prompt_templates.title: Compare MCP Setup Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare CoinGecko public, authenticated, and local MCP server options for my use case: [workflow and expected volume].

prompt_templates.title: Review an Integration Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my CoinGecko integration plan for [application]. Check endpoint selection, API key handling, rate limits, retries, and data freshness.

output_examples.input: Which CoinGecko endpoint should I use to show Bitcoin and Ethereum prices in USD?
output_examples.output: Use the simple price endpoint with coin IDs for Bitcoin and Ethereum, and set USD as the target currency. Add your API key through the recommended header method when using an authenticated plan.

output_examples.input: I want Claude Code to access CoinGecko through MCP. Which setup should I choose?
output_examples.output: Use the public remote server for quick testing. Use the authenticated remote server or local server when you need higher limits, plan-specific tools, or controlled key handling.

output_examples.input: Review my plan to query onchain pool data every minute.
output_examples.output: Check that your endpoint matches the network and pool address. Confirm your plan limits, cache frequency, retry behavior, and API key storage before scheduling repeated requests.

best_practices: Use headers for API keys when the endpoint supports them.
Confirm endpoint availability against your CoinGecko plan before implementation.
Handle rate limits, stale data, and failed requests explicitly.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode real API keys in prompts, source files, or shared logs.
Do not assume public and Pro API base URLs are interchangeable.
Do not treat cryptocurrency market data output as investment advice.

faq.answer: No. It provides documentation and guidance for building integrations.

faq.question: Can it help with Pro API authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Pro API key usage, headers, query parameters, and secure storage guidance.

faq.question: Does it cover MCP setup?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes public, authenticated, and local CoinGecko MCP server options.

faq.question: Can it generate application code?
faq.answer: It can guide coding agents with documented patterns, but generated code should still be reviewed and tested.

faq.question: Does it include NFT and onchain data?
faq.answer: Yes. The references include NFT, exchange, trending, and GeckoTerminal onchain endpoint information.

faq.answer: No. It is technical API documentation support only.
